f.title: Adhere to authority-set matters during a safety monitoring period
f.statement: Where the central competent health authority sets a specific safety monitoring period for a medicament approved for manufacture or import, pharmaceutical firms shall adhere to the matters the authority establishes for that period (the authority's power to set the period is discretionary: 'may').
f.applicability: Taiwan; official English translation from the Laws & Regulations Database (Chinese text prevails). Only PV-relevant provisions captured. Implemented by the Regulations for the Management of Drug Safety Surveillance.

rows.actor: Pharmaceutical firm (manufacture or import approval holder)
rows.quote:
The central competent health authority may set a specific period for monitoring the safety of the medicaments approved for manufacture or import.
The central competent health authority shall establish matters that the pharmaceutical firms shall adhere to during the safety monitoring period referred to in the preceding paragraph.
rows.review_note: Review: statement re-centred on the firm's duty to adhere to the matters set for the monitoring period (setting the period is the authority's 'may'); accountable changed from governance-3 to governance-1 (QPPV) for PV system obligations. Double-check: quote proves the firm duty to adhere to the matters set for the monitoring period; content of those matters sits in the DSS Regulations; English translation, so held below 90 per GUIDE.

f.title: Report serious adverse reactions caused by medicaments
f.statement: Medical care institutions, pharmacies and pharmaceutical firms shall report any serious adverse reactions caused by medicaments; reporting method, content and other matters are set by regulations of the central competent health authority.
f.applicability: Taiwan; official English translation from the Laws & Regulations Database (Chinese text prevails). Only PV-relevant provisions captured. Implemented by the Regulations for Reporting Serious Adverse Reactions of Medicaments.

rows.quote: Medical care institutions, pharmacies, and pharmaceutical firms shall report any serious adverse reactions caused by medicaments. Regulations regarding reporting method, content, and other matters to be complied with shall be established by the central competent health authority.
rows.review_note: Review: no change (applicability wording tidied). Double-check: quote proves actor, modal and duty; method and timing are delegated to the serious ADR Regulations; English translation, so held below 90 per GUIDE.

f.title: Obtain approval before altering registered particulars
f.statement: No alteration may be made to any originally registered particulars of an approved medicament without approval of the central competent health authority.
f.applicability: Taiwan; official English translation from the Laws & Regulations Database (Chinese text prevails). Only PV-relevant provisions captured.

rows.quote: Without approval of the central competent health authority, no alteration may be made to any of the originally registered particulars pertaining to any medicament approved for manufacture or import.
rows.review_note: Review: kept; PV relevance is that safety label changes to registered particulars need prior approval. Article 46(2) transfer registration not captured (not PV). Double-check: passive provision, actor (license holder) inferred; PV relevance (safety label changes) is an interpretation; English translation, so held below 90 per GUIDE.

f.title: Rectify safety or efficacy concerns within the time limit when ordered after re-evaluation
f.statement: Where the central competent health authority re-evaluates and confirms a safety or medical efficacy concern during the validity period of the manufacture or import license and orders the pharmaceutical firm to rectify it within a time limit, the firm shall make the corrections within that time limit; failure to do so results in revocation of the license. Ordering rectification is at the authority's discretion ('may'), and where there is a serious safety concern the authority may revoke the license directly.
f.applicability: Taiwan; official English translation from the Laws & Regulations Database (Chinese text prevails). Only PV-relevant provisions captured.
f.exceptions: Applies only when the authority issues a rectification order; for a serious safety concern the authority may revoke the license directly without a rectification opportunity.

rows.actor: Pharmaceutical firm (license holder), when ordered by the central competent health authority
rows.deadline: Within the time limit set in the authority's order
rows.quote: If there is a safety or medical efficacy concern of medicaments as re-evaluated and confirmed by the central competent health authority within the validity period of the manufacture or import license, pharmaceutical firms may be ordered to rectify any concerns within a time limit. For those who fail to make corrections within the given time limit, their licenses shall be revoked. Where there is a serious safety concern, the central competent health authority may revoke the license directly.
rows.review_note: Review: Article 48 ordering rectification is an authority 'may'; the firm's duty is to comply with an order once issued (sanction: license revocation), so the row is restated as a conditional duty to comply and kept Mandatory; authority discretion and direct revocation moved to exceptions/statement. Double-check: Mandatory accepted: statement is framed as the firm duty to correct once ordered and the quote supports it through the sanction (licenses shall be revoked on failure to correct). Duty is inferred from the sanction rather than stated; English translation, so held below 90 per GUIDE.

f.title: Handle unused specially approved drugs within the time limit when ordered for safety or efficacy concerns
f.statement: Where the central competent health authority revokes a special approval granted under Article 48-2(1) (no domestic alternative for life-threatening or severely disabling diseases, or emergency/major public health need), including because the drug was reviewed and considered to raise safety or medical efficacy concerns, it may, if necessary, order the applicant to handle unused drugs within a prescribed time limit and may publicly announce their recall. When so ordered, the applicant must handle the unused drugs within that time limit (duty inferred from the order; the Article states no separate sanction).
f.applicability: Taiwan; official English translation from the Laws & Regulations Database (Chinese text prevails). Only PV-relevant provisions captured. Drugs specially approved under Article 48-2(1).
f.exceptions: Applies only if the authority revokes the special approval and orders handling of unused drugs.

rows.actor: Applicant/holder of a special approval under Article 48-2, when ordered by the central competent health authority
rows.deadline: Within the time limit prescribed by the authority
rows.quote:
Where any of the following circumstances occur, the central competent health authority may revoke the approval granted in the preceding paragraph; if necessary, may order the applicants to handle unused drugs within a prescribed time limit, and may publicly announce the recall thereof:
I. Where a drug obtains market approval for registration or an appropriate treatment becomes available corresponding to the circumstance prescribed in Subparagraph 1 of the preceding paragraph.
II. Where the emergency or major public health circumstance has been terminated.
III. Where the drug was reviewed and considered with concerns about its safety or medical efficacy by the central competent health authority.
rows.review_note: Review: added (missed). Article 48-2(2) authority 'may' revoke special approvals and order handling of unused drugs, incl. on safety/efficacy concern (III); firm's duty is to comply once ordered, treated like Article 48. Double-check: Mandatory kept as a judgement call: the quote only gives the authority power to order handling of unused drugs and states no duty or sanction for the applicant, so the duty to comply is inferred from the order. Statement restated around the applicant duty when ordered; English translation, so held below 90 per GUIDE.

f.title: Show adverse reactions, contraindications, warnings and precautions on labeling as approved
f.statement: The labels, use instructions and packaging of medicaments shall indicate, as approved, particulars including adverse reactions, contraindications, and other warnings and precautions.
f.applicability: Taiwan; official English translation from the Laws & Regulations Database (Chinese text prevails). Only PV-relevant provisions captured.

rows.review_note: Review: no change. Quote stops at item 7 (items 1-6 and 8 not PV-specific); Article 75(3) Braille measures not captured (not PV). Double-check: passive provision, actor (license holder) inferred; quote is a list cut after item 7 (item 8 omitted as non-PV); English translation, so held below 90 per GUIDE.

f.title: Stop distribution of medicaments prohibited for serious hazards within the time limit
f.statement: Where a medicament approved for manufacture or import is found to cause serious hazards, the central competent health authority shall at any time announce a prohibition of its manufacture or import and revoke the license. Medicaments already manufactured or imported are prohibited, within a time limit, from export, dispensation, sale, supply, transport, storage, brokerage, transfer or display with intent to sell, and may be confiscated and destroyed if necessary.
f.applicability: Taiwan; official English translation from the Laws & Regulations Database (Chinese text prevails). Only PV-relevant provisions captured. Medicaments found to cause serious hazards and prohibited by announcement; links to the recall duty in Article 80(1)(I).

rows.actor: Pharmaceutical firm (license holder) and other holders of the medicament
rows.deadline: Within the time limit set in the prohibition
rows.quote: In case any medicament approved for manufacture or import is found to cause serious hazards, the central competent health authority shall, at any time, announce prohibiting its manufacture or import and further revoke the medicament license. As for those medicaments that have already been manufactured or imported, they shall be prohibited from export, dispensation, sale, supply, transport, storage, brokerage, transfer, or display with intent to sell within a time limit. Such medicaments may be confiscated and destroyed if necessary.
rows.review_note: Review: added (missed). Article 76 safety-driven prohibition: products already made or imported must be taken out of distribution within the time limit. Double-check: scope checked: statement keeps the authority duty (announce prohibition, revoke license) as context and the passive prohibition on further distribution within a time limit; actor (license holder and other holders) is inferred from the passive wording, and the cross-link to Article 80(1)(I) recall is an applicability note, not quoted; English translation, so held below 90 per GUIDE.

f.title: Notify and recall medicaments that damage or may damage users
f.statement: If a medicament falls under the listed circumstances (including a licensed medicament later prohibited by announcement, or medicaments found after inspection to be damaging or likely to damage the life, body or health of users, or other recalls announced by the authority), its manufacturer or importer shall immediately notify medical care institutions, pharmacies and pharmaceutical firms and, within a prescribed time limit, recall and dispose of it.
f.applicability: Taiwan; official English translation from the Laws & Regulations Database (Chinese text prevails). Only PV-relevant provisions captured. Circumstances I-VI of Article 80(1), e.g. I: licensed medicament later prohibited by announcement; IV: medicaments found after inspection to be damaging or likely to damage users; VI: recalls announced by the authority. Recall classification and handling are set by separate regulations (Article 80(3)).

rows.deadline: Notify immediately; recall within the prescribed time limit
rows.quote: If any of the following circumstances apply to any medicament, its manufacturer or importer shall immediately notify medical care institutions, pharmacies, and pharmaceutical firms and, within a prescribed time limit, shall recall the medicament in question from the market and dispose of it together with its stock of the medicament pursuant to the relevant provisions of this Act:
rows.review_note: Review: applicability adds circumstance I and the Article 80(3) implementing regulations; otherwise no change. Double-check: quote proves the actor, immediacy and recall duty but ends at the lead-in colon, so the circumstances I-VI in applicability are not in the quote; English translation, so held below 90 per GUIDE.

f.title: Cooperate with manufacturers or importers in recalling medicaments
f.statement: Medical care institutions, pharmacies and pharmaceutical firms shall cooperate with manufacturers or importers in recalling medicaments that fall under the circumstances of Article 80(1).
f.applicability: Taiwan; official English translation from the Laws & Regulations Database (Chinese text prevails). Only PV-relevant provisions captured. Recalls under Article 80(1).
f.processes: Risk management & minimisation; Partner & vendor oversight

rows.actor: Pharmaceutical firm (including distributors), medical care institutions and pharmacies
rows.quote: Medical care institutions, pharmacies, and pharmaceutical firms shall cooperate with manufacturers or importers in recalling the medicaments set forth in the subparagraphs of the preceding paragraph.
rows.review_note: Review: added (missed). Article 80(2) duty to cooperate in recalls applies to pharmaceutical firms acting as distributors or partners. Double-check: quote proves the cooperation duty and actors; RACI mapping to partners/supply liaison is an operating-model judgement; English translation, so held below 90 per GUIDE.
